title: Error Handling Unit Operation Execution Contract

scope.component: Step Supporting Error Handling Unit operation-execution protocol
scope.purpose: Define the detailed callable, input, operation-result, attempt identity, target-occurrence access, and publication protocol of an Error Handling Unit that conforms to Step_Supporting_Error_Handling_Unit_Contract.json.
scope.normativeBoundary: This document refines operation execution and publication mechanics. The common Supporting Unit role, association scope, invocation provenance, and lifecycle authority are governed by the Step_Supporting_Error_Handling_Unit Behavioral, Association, and Lifecycle Contracts.

contract.name: ErrorHandlingUnit
contract.role: A Step-owned executable collaborator that performs one or more authorized handling operations and publishes one structured operation entry for each operation execution that produces a result, under the broader Supporting Error Handling Unit contract.
contract.executionMeaning: One invocation may contain multiple distinct Handling Operation Attempts. Each attempt must obtain its own PublicationReservation before the operation begins. Each operation execution that produces a structured THandlingOperationResult is represented by one entry and published under the reservation bound to that attempt. Accepted entries remain retained independently of later normal or exceptional invocation termination.
contract.ownership: The Error Handling Unit is a Step-owned pluggable collaborator. Step Composition owns its association and lifecycle; it may be associated with a particular SPU without transferring orchestration ownership to that SPU.
nonResponsibilities: Define or register SPUErrorTypeDefinition values or own the Pipeline-assigned SPUErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry.
Create, replace, mutate, or own SPUError occurrences.
Own the ErrorResult aggregate or change its contents.
Own or assemble the final StepExecutionResult.
Impose a universal handling policy, outcome taxonomy, retry policy, or resolution guarantee.
Convert thrown exceptions automatically into operation results.
contract.stepSpecializationRequirement: Every Step using this Unit and Publisher must concretely define protocol result types, no-fail result-transfer representation, Publisher Contract Violation Recovery Owner/procedure, identity generation, and status retention in its own contract conforming to 01.02_Step_Error_Handling/Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract.json.

typeParameters.name: TErrorHandlingUnitInput
typeParameters.meaning: The Step-specialized input accepted by one invocation of this Error Handling Unit.
typeParameters.specialization: Defined by the owning Step and the concrete Error Handling Unit. It provides the operation context and, for occurrence-targeted operations, controlled access to the candidate SPUError occurrences that the unit is permitted to inspect or target. No universal input class or field layout is imposed.

typeParameters.name: THandlingOperationResult
typeParameters.meaning: The structured result type produced by one actual handling operation performed by this Error Handling Unit.
typeParameters.specialization: Defined by the concrete Error Handling Unit within the owning Step. It describes the operation-specific result or evidence and is not the result of the entire Error Handling Unit invocation.

operationResultSpecialization.principle: THandlingOperationResult is specialized per concrete Error Handling Unit and represents one operation execution.
minimumSemanticRequirements: Represent the result of one actual operation execution, not an operation plan, declared handling action, or entire unit invocation.
Carry the operation-specific information required by the owning Step to interpret what the operation produced.
Remain associated with the corresponding handlingOperationIdentity and target occurrence references through ErrorHandlingOperationEntry.
Preserve all operation-specific evidence or data required by the Step's handling and audit semantics.
Be a structured result type; a bare success Boolean is insufficient unless the Step-specific contract explicitly defines why that Boolean is the complete required result.
stepSpecificSpecializationMayDefine: An operation-specific outcome classification or status, if meaningful for that operation.
What action was actually performed and what observable effect or evidence resulted.
Diagnostics, reason codes, or operation-specific failure details when the operation returns such a result.
Retry, compensation, or follow-up information when required by the Step's own policy.
Any typed payload needed to communicate the operation result to the Step-specific composition.
constraints: No common success, failure, handled, resolved, ignored, retried, or compensated field is mandated.
Producing an operation result does not imply that the targeted occurrence has been resolved.
An operation that throws before producing THandlingOperationResult does not produce an operation entry by implication.

When multiple Error Handling Units use different result types, the Step-specific THandlingOperationEntry must preserve the concrete result type and its association with the producing unit; a tagged union, variant, or another Step-defined heterogeneous representation may be used.

inputAndOccurrenceAccess.inputPrinciple: The Error Handling Unit receives Step-specialized input containing the authorized invocation and Association context, operation context, and bounded target-occurrence/resource access required by its assigned operations.

semanticInputCapabilities.name: associationContext
semanticInputCapabilities.requirement: The input identifies the exact Step-owned Association selected by Step Composition and its bound associationTargetIdentity.
constraints: The association context includes stepInstanceIdentity, errorHandlingUnitIdentity, errorHandlingUnitAssociationIdentity, and associationTargetIdentity.
The Unit invocation is bound to exactly one Association; the Unit must not infer or substitute another Association.
The association target identifies the authorized applicability scope and is not necessarily the exact target occurrence/resource of each operation.

semanticInputCapabilities.name: operationContext
semanticInputCapabilities.requirement: The input provides the Step-specific context needed to select and perform the unit's operations. Its structure is defined by the Step.

semanticInputCapabilities.name: targetOccurrenceAccess
semanticInputCapabilities.requirement: For operations that target SPUError occurrences, the input provides a bounded, read-only way to enumerate or select eligible occurrences and inspect the occurrence information permitted to the unit.
constraints: The access surface identifies occurrences using producerSPUIdentity plus occurrenceIdentity.
The access surface resolves references to the original occurrences or to faithful read-only views of those occurrences; it does not manufacture replacement occurrences.
The unit may target only occurrences made available under the Step-specific input and selection rules.
The unit does not gain ownership of the source occurrences or permission to mutate ErrorResult through this access surface.
A Step may omit occurrence access for an explicitly non-occurrence-targeted operation.

semanticInputCapabilities.name: unitConfiguration
semanticInputCapabilities.requirement: The Step may provide configuration or dependencies required by the concrete unit. Their types, ownership, and lifetime are Step-specific.

accessLifetime: Any invocation-scoped resolved occurrence view or access handle is valid only for the lifetime guaranteed by the input contract.
The Error Handling Unit must not retain a raw pointer, reference, or borrowed view beyond that lifetime unless the Step-specific contract explicitly supplies an owning or lifetime-pinning handle.
The operation entry retains identity references, not borrowed occurrence pointers.

operationEntryPublication.publisherOwner: The Step-specific Error Handling Composition owns and supplies the Publisher capability for the Invocation.
attemptProtocol: Create a new handlingOperationAttemptIdentity for the intended operation attempt; this identity does not assert that execution has started.
Call reserve(handlingOperationAttemptIdentity) and do not begin the operation unless a valid PublicationReservation is granted.
After grant and before operation start, assign a new handlingOperationIdentity to the actual execution. One attempt may start at most one actual execution.
Execute the operation and produce its specialized THandlingOperationResult.
If the operation will not produce a result, release the unused reservation. A normal return or exception does not implicitly release it.
If a result is produced, preserve it locally, prepare the complete ErrorHandlingOperationEntry, and call publish with the same reservation.
The entry carries handlingOperationAttemptIdentity as well as handlingOperationIdentity, allowing the Publisher to validate the reservation-to-entry binding.

Every complete operation entry preserves stepInstanceIdentity, errorHandlingUnitAssociationIdentity, associationTargetIdentity, and errorHandlingInvocationIdentity in addition to Unit, attempt, operation, target-occurrence, and result data.
publicationSemantics: The complete entry is prepared before publish is invoked. The Step-specific type/transfer contract must provide a non-throwing final ownership handoff, either directly or through an already-prepared owning envelope/handle.
Calling publish does not transfer retention responsibility. Responsibility transfers only at the Publisher atomic-acceptance point.
PublicationAccepted means the complete entry is retained and the reservation is Consumed.
A PublicationRejection means no acceptance occurred; the Unit retains responsibility for any produced result.
A Publisher Contract Violation is distinct from ordinary rejection and must not be relabeled as a normal publication rejection.

If publish throws or its acknowledgement is not observed, the Unit preserves the result and reservation and queries get_publication_status. Consumed means accepted; Reserved permits retrying the same logical entry; Released while a produced result is pending indicates a contract violation.
A retry after ambiguous publication reuses the same reservation and same logical entry. It must not create a new operation execution or a second entry.
An idempotent retry of the same already-accepted entry returns acknowledgement for the original acceptance without duplicate retention.
Each reservation authorizes one entry for one attempt only. The Publisher retains accepted entries independently of later execute termination.
The Publisher is the authoritative delivery path; the Unit does not also return a collection of operation entries.
The entry provenance fields must match the exact Step/Association/target/invocation binding of the invocation-scoped Publisher and its reservation.
ownershipAndLifetime: The composition owns the Publisher and its accepted-entry storage; the Unit temporarily uses the Publisher as an invocation-scoped capability.
Before atomic acceptance, the Unit retains responsibility for the produced result and prepared entry.
After atomic acceptance, the Publisher/Composition retains the complete entry for Step-specific collection and aggregation.
Publication does not transfer ownership of the Unit or source SPUError occurrences and does not mutate ErrorResult.
failurePreservation: An exception before result production does not create a synthetic entry; if no result exists, the Unit releases the reservation under the release preconditions.

An exception after result production but before acceptance does not permit discarding the result or releasing its reservation. The Unit retains the result and follows the Step-specific publication recovery path.
An exception after atomic acceptance does not revoke acceptance. If acknowledgement was not observed, status lookup resolves the outcome where the Publisher is available.
Failure of status lookup does not prove rejection and does not authorize discarding the result or starting a replacement execution.

The Unit and Step-specific Composition must ensure that every produced result remains owned by the Unit before acceptance or by the Publisher/Composition after acceptance, unless an explicit Step-specific recovery owner takes responsibility.

If execute unwinds exceptionally while a produced result remains unpublished, the Step-specific contract must expose the complete pending result/entry to the composition through an explicit recovery envelope, exception payload, or invocation-scoped recovery record. Merely retaining it in a Unit-local variable that becomes unreachable on unwind is insufficient.
The concrete Recovery Owner, recovery record/envelope type, custody-transfer operation, and reconciliation/escalation procedure are mandatory Step contract definitions.

callableExecutionContract.return: None; normal return indicates that the invocation completed normally, not that no operation results exist.
rules: Each Handling Operation Attempt receives a distinct handlingOperationAttemptIdentity before its reservation request.
The Unit must obtain a valid PublicationReservation before beginning the corresponding Handling Operation.
A rejected reservation means that operation attempt must not begin; a later execution retry requires a new attempt identity and reservation.
After reservation grant and before operation start, the Unit assigns handlingOperationIdentity to the actual execution. One attempt starts at most one actual execution.

Each operation execution that produces a structured THandlingOperationResult is represented by one entry carrying handler identity, attempt identity, operation identity, target references, and operation result.
The Unit prepares the complete entry and publishes it using the reservation bound to the same attempt.
The invocation may contain zero or multiple attempts and may publish zero or multiple accepted entries; zero entries do not by themselves mean failure.
The Unit does not return a competing collection of operation entries and does not construct ErrorHandlerResult unless the Step explicitly assigns that responsibility.
The Unit does not assemble StepExecutionResult.
Every operation entry published by the invocation carries the same errorHandlingInvocationIdentity and the exact Association context authorized for that invocation.
exceptionBoundary: An exception before THandlingOperationResult production does not create a synthetic operation entry; the unused reservation is released only if the operation produced no result and no entry is pending.
If an exception occurs after result production but before atomic publication acceptance, the Unit retains the result and reservation and must not treat the result as absent.

If an exception occurs after atomic acceptance but before acknowledgement observation, the Unit uses get_publication_status to reconcile the publication state; absence of acknowledgement is not proof of rejection.
An exception thrown by Publisher infrastructure that violates a granted reservation is a Publisher Contract Violation, distinct from a normal PublicationRejection.
The Unit-specific exception behavior and local recovery remain Step-specialized. No common conversion of exceptions into THandlingOperationResult is imposed.
callableExecutionContract.executionMode: Synchronous/asynchronous behavior is selected by the owning Step contract; this document does not impose one execution mode.

errorHandlingUnitIdentity.identifies: One concrete Error Handling Unit runtime instance within its owning Step instance, independently of the target scopes to which it may be associated.
errorHandlingUnitIdentity.assignedBy: Step Composition or an identity provider supplied by it when the Unit instance is created or admitted into the Step's internal component composition.
errorHandlingUnitIdentity.uniquenessScope: Unique within the owning Step instance for as long as any invocation, operation entry, recovery record, or aggregate carrying that identity may be observed. It is not scoped to a particular SPU association.
stability: Stable for the lifetime of that Error Handling Unit runtime instance, regardless of the number or kinds of Associations it has.
A newly created replacement instance receives a new identity while results from the prior instance may still be observed.
A reused instance retains its identity across invocations and association changes during its lifetime.
errorHandlingUnitIdentity.generation: The Step defines the identity representation and generation mechanism. It must prevent collisions within the stated uniqueness scope; no UUID, counter, timestamp, or other specific mechanism is mandated.
errorHandlingUnitIdentity.ownership: Step Composition is authoritative for assignment within the owning Step identity scope; the Unit receives and retains the assigned identity.

handlingOperationIdentity.identifies: One actual Handling Operation execution that began after a valid PublicationReservation was granted.
handlingOperationIdentity.assignedBy: The Error Handling Unit, or an identity provider explicitly supplied to it by the owning SPU/Step composition.
handlingOperationIdentity.uniquenessScope: Unique within the lifetime and identity scope of its producing Error Handling Unit instance.
stability: Assigned only after the attempt receives a valid reservation and before the actual operation begins.
A reservation-rejected attempt has no handlingOperationIdentity because no execution began.
One Handling Operation Attempt starts at most one actual execution.
A distinct execution retry requires a new handlingOperationAttemptIdentity and receives a new handlingOperationIdentity.
An ambiguous publication retry reuses the existing operation identity because it republishes the same execution result.
handlingOperationIdentity.generation: The concrete unit or its supplied identity provider selects the mechanism. It must preserve uniqueness under the concurrency model permitted by the Step.
handlingOperationIdentity.compositeIdentity: The pair errorHandlingUnitIdentity plus handlingOperationIdentity uniquely identifies an operation entry within the applicable SPU identity scope.

scopeLimit: These identities are runtime identities within the defined SPU/unit lifetime scopes; global uniqueness across process restarts or durable persistence is not implied.
If a Step needs cross-process or durable identity, it must define the additional execution or persistence scope explicitly.
Identity values must not be inferred from operation results, target occurrences, operation kinds, or wall-clock timestamps alone.

handlingOperationAttemptIdentity.identifies: One distinct attempt to obtain authorization and begin a Handling Operation. An attempt may be rejected before execution begins.
handlingOperationAttemptIdentity.assignedBy: The Error Handling Unit or an identity provider supplied by the owning SPU/Step composition, before calling Publisher.reserve.
handlingOperationAttemptIdentity.uniquenessScope: Unique within the lifetime/identity scope of its producing Error Handling Unit instance for as long as any attempt, reservation, or result entry carrying it may be observed.
stability: Assigned before reservation request and unchanged throughout the attempt.
A reservation rejection does not create a handlingOperationIdentity.
A retry intended to begin a new execution uses a new attempt identity.
An ambiguous publication retry for the same already-executed attempt reuses the same attempt identity and reservation.
handlingOperationAttemptIdentity.compositeAssociation: The reservation is bound to this attempt identity; the published entry carries it alongside the actual handlingOperationIdentity.
handlingOperationAttemptIdentity.generation: The Step defines the representation and generation mechanism; it must prevent collisions under permitted concurrency.

errorHandlingInvocationIdentity.identifies: One invocation of one Error Handling Unit runtime instance under one selected Association.
errorHandlingInvocationIdentity.assignedBy: Step Composition or an identity provider supplied by it before the Unit invocation begins.
errorHandlingInvocationIdentity.uniquenessScope: Unique within the owning Step identity scope for as long as any operation entry, recovery record, publication status, or aggregate may refer to the invocation.
binding: Bound to exactly one errorHandlingUnitIdentity and errorHandlingUnitAssociationIdentity.
Carries the corresponding associationTargetIdentity and stepInstanceIdentity.
All operation attempts and entries produced by the same invocation carry this identity.
A repeated invocation receives a new identity even when the same Unit instance and Association are reused.
errorHandlingInvocationIdentity.generation: The concrete Step defines representation and generation; uniqueness must hold under the Step concurrency and retention model.

targetCardinality.default: One or more target occurrence references per occurrence-targeted operation entry.
stepSpecificRefinements: A Step may narrow the cardinality to exactly one occurrence for single-occurrence operations.
A Step may define a bounded or otherwise constrained number of occurrences for batch operations.
A Step may retain one-or-more semantics for operations that can process a variable-sized group.

zeroTargetException.permitted: Only when the Step explicitly defines an operation whose target is not an SPUError occurrence, such as a Step-scoped or context-scoped handling operation.
zeroTargetException.requiredSafeguard: The Step-specialized entry or its THandlingOperationResult/TErrorHandlingContext must identify the non-occurrence target scope unambiguously. An empty target collection without an explicitly defined alternative target scope is invalid.
zeroTargetException.meaning: A zero-target operation is not treated as having implicitly targeted every occurrence.

multipleOperations: One operation may target multiple occurrences.
Multiple distinct operations may target the same occurrence.
The same occurrence reference must not be duplicated within one operation entry unless the Step explicitly assigns a distinct meaning to repeated targeting.
targetCardinality.enforcement: The owning Step defines and validates the concrete cardinality for each operation kind. This contract supplies the default, not a universal restriction that overrides Step-specific semantics.

occurrenceReferenceLifetimeAndResolution.referenceIdentity: HandledErrorOccurrenceReference consists of producerSPUIdentity plus occurrenceIdentity, as defined by Step_Error_Model_Contract.json.
occurrenceReferenceLifetimeAndResolution.referenceNature: The reference is an identity value, not an owning pointer and not a copy of the occurrence.
duringInvocation: The SPU makes eligible original occurrences available to the Error Handling Unit through its Step-specialized input/access surface.
The unit selects and records references only to occurrences available in that invocation's authorized access scope.
The access surface resolves a selected reference to the original occurrence or a faithful read-only view while its validity guarantee holds.
afterInvocation: If ErrorResult is present and contains the referenced occurrence, the reference resolves against that original occurrence entry using producerSPUIdentity plus occurrenceIdentity.

If ErrorResult is absent or does not contain the occurrence, post-invocation resolution is guaranteed only when the Step retains and exposes a separate occurrence-resolution scope or another explicitly defined stable resolution mechanism.
If no such resolution mechanism is retained, the reference remains a correlation identity only; dereferencing occurrence content after the invocation is not guaranteed.
The ErrorHandlerResult does not own the occurrence and does not extend its lifetime merely by storing the identity reference.
lifetimeGuarantees: The source occurrence must remain valid for the duration of any Error Handling Unit operation that is inspecting it.
The Step defines whether occurrence data remains resolvable after the SPU invocation and for how long.

If post-invocation resolution is required while ErrorResult is absent, the Step-specific TErrorHandlingContext or an associated handle must identify and retain the required resolution scope without embedding ErrorResult.
A Step must not promise post-invocation dereferencing if its source occurrence storage has already been released.
No raw pointer or borrowed reference may be used as a substitute for the composite identity in a stored ErrorHandlerResult.
occurrenceReferenceLifetimeAndResolution.independence: ErrorResult and ErrorHandlerResult remain independently optional. Their independent optionality does not imply that every occurrence reference is always dereferenceable after the invocation.

lifecycleAndComposition.lifecycleOwner: The owning Step Composition controls association, provisioning, invocation coordination, collection, reuse, and release of Error Handling Unit instances. A Unit may be associated with a particular SPU, but that association does not transfer orchestration or lifecycle ownership to the SPU.
lifecycleAndComposition.lifecyclePolicy: Defined per Step and per Error Handling Unit. The unit may be invocation-scoped or reused across multiple invocations according to the Step's design.

conceptualPhases.responsibility: Step Composition creates or obtains the Unit, establishes any SPU association required by the Step design, and assigns errorHandlingUnitIdentity.
The Unit receives or establishes the dependencies and configuration required by its own contract.

The composition supplies specialized input and an invocation-bound Publisher capability. For each operation, the Unit creates an attempt identity, obtains a reservation, then starts execution only after grant.
Step Composition reconciles publication outcomes and collects accepted entries independently of normal or exceptional Unit termination.

Step Composition releases or retains the Unit according to Step-specific policy. Unused reservations are released only when no result requiring publication exists; pending produced results prevent normal Invocation closure.

compositionRules: The Step Composition determines applicable Units, their association with SPUs or Step scope, invocation timing, operation selection, sequential/concurrent execution, and semantic operation ordering.
The Step Composition supplies an invocation-bound Publisher that implements OperationEntryPublisher_Contract.json.
Each operation attempt requires its own reservation before execution; the Publisher does not schedule operations.
The Step Composition retains and aggregates every accepted entry without merging distinct executions.
The Step Composition reconciles uncertain publication outcomes using reservation status and does not infer rejection from a missing acknowledgement.
Invocation closure is not complete while a produced result remains unpublished or a granted reservation remains unresolved.

The Step-specific Error Handling Composition constructs ErrorHandlerResult when at least one operation entry is selected for inclusion; if no entries are produced, no empty ErrorHandlerResult is required.
Step Composition integrates ErrorHandlerResult into StepExecutionResult and returns the final StepExecutionResult.
notMandated: No universal constructor, dependency-injection mechanism, factory, pool, or service locator is prescribed.
No universal initialize/dispose method names or interface shape is prescribed.
No universal operation scheduling policy, execution concurrency level, semantic ordering, reentrancy, cancellation, or timeout behavior is prescribed; these remain Step-specific.
No universal Unit reuse scope is prescribed.

rules: Each operation entry preserves errorHandlingUnitIdentity, handlingOperationIdentity, targetOccurrenceReferences, and THandlingOperationResult.
The Error Handling Unit publishes operation entries through the composition-owned publisher; the Step-specific composition aggregates accepted entries into the Step-specialized ErrorHandlerResult.
Step Composition integrates ErrorHandlerResult as the independent optional errorHandlerResult element of StepExecutionResult.
ErrorHandlerResult does not contain, mutate, remove, or subsume ErrorResult.

ConcreteSPU: Make SPUError occurrences produced by its own processing responsibility available to Step Composition with producer and occurrence identities preserved.
Provide SPU-specific context or authorized occurrence access to an Error Handling Unit only when Step Composition assigns that interaction to the SPU.
ErrorHandlingUnit: Perform the operations assigned by the Step design.
Select only authorized target occurrences through the supplied access surface.
Generate or obtain a unique handlingOperationIdentity for each distinct operation execution.
Produce the specialized THandlingOperationResult for each operation and publish its corresponding operation entry through the supplied publisher.
Publish operation entries through the supplied composition-owned publisher without changing source occurrences or ErrorResult.
StepSpecificErrorHandlingComposition: Operate as a Step-owned composition capability coordinated by Step Composition.
Implement the Step-defined selection, invocation, collection, recovery/reconciliation, and aggregation policy.
Preserve heterogeneous operation result types and all operation/target identities.
PipelineAndStage: Pipeline does not own or globally coordinate Error Handling Unit instances through the error-type Registry mechanism.
Stage Composition does not prescribe Step-internal Error Handling Unit selection, lifecycle, or operation policy.
StepComposition: Own the association and lifecycle/reuse decisions for Error Handling Unit instances, including units associated with a particular SPU.
Provide each Unit with its Step-specialized input, authorized target-occurrence access, and invocation-bound Publisher.
Coordinate operation-entry collection and recovery/reconciliation of uncertain publication outcomes.
Aggregate accepted operation entries into ErrorHandlerResult according to the Step-specific composition contract.

explicitNonGoals: No universal operation status or error-resolution semantics.
No global Error Handling Unit registry or central handling gateway.
No mandatory one-unit-per-occurrence or one-operation-per-invocation rule.
No mandatory persistent or cross-process occurrence-reference resolution.
No implicit extension of source occurrence lifetime by ErrorHandlerResult.
No universal lifecycle or dependency-injection framework.
No universal publisher concurrency, ordering, or publication-infrastructure failure policy is imposed.

openDesignDetails: Define concrete TErrorHandlingUnitInput and THandlingOperationResult types for each actual Error Handling Unit introduced by a Step.
Define concrete TErrorHandlingContext for each Step, including whether it carries a post-invocation occurrence-resolution handle.
Define occurrence-resolution retention duration and ownership for Steps that require post-invocation resolution when ErrorResult is absent.
Define per-operation target cardinality and explicit non-occurrence target scopes for each concrete handling operation.
Define the lifecycle scope, dependency provision, cleanup, reuse, and concurrency guarantees for each concrete Error Handling Unit.

Every concrete Step must instantiate the protocol type, transfer, recovery, identity, and status-retention obligations in 01.02_Step_Error_Handling/Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract.json; these are mandatory Step contract content.
